- **self**: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler (27/11)

## Definitions

- [statement] A Compound III (Comet) deployment is an isolated market with exactly one borrowable base asset (the original market is USDC on Ethereum, cUSDCv3). Users post other listed assets as collateral and borrow only the base asset; only base-asset suppliers earn interest. (high confidence) — https://docs.compound.xyz/ · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://docs.compound.xyz/collateral-and-borrowing/, https://blockworks.com/token-transparency/filing/compound, https://defilending.substack.com/p/special-issue-a-deep-dive-into-compound
- [statement] Comet is a small set of contracts. The Comet core (inherits CometMainInterface) forwards unrecognised function selectors to CometExt by delegatecall; the Configurator (behind a TransparentUpgradeableProxy-derived ConfiguratorProxy) holds configuration and deploys new Comet implementations through CometFactory; CometProxyAdmin adds deployAndUpgradeTo, which deploys a new Comet and upgrades the proxy in one transaction; Bulker batches calls and CometRewards handles reward claims. (high confidence) — https://github.com/compound-finance/comet · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://docs.compound.xyz/governance/

## Structure and components

- [statement] Euler v2 has two layers. The Euler Vault Kit (EVK) builds 'credit vaults': ERC-4626 vaults with added borrowing functionality that act as passive lending pools and do not invest deposits. The Ethereum Vault Connector (EVC) is a foundational layer between vaults: the EVC is responsible for authentication and vaults for authorisation, and each vault holds a single asset. (high confidence) — https://github.com/euler-xyz/euler-vault-kit · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/euler-vault-kit/master/docs/whitepaper.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/ethereum-vault-connector/master/docs/whitepaper.md, https://mixbytes.io/blog/modern-defi-lending-protocols-how-its-made-euler-v2
- [statement] Morpho Blue is the EVM baseline for where state lives. One singleton contract keeps every position in a storage mapping, `mapping(Id => mapping(address => Position)) public position`, and its README calls the protocol a 'simple, immutable, and governance-minimized base layer'. (high confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue/main/src/Morpho.sol · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue/main/README.md
- [statement] Jupiter Lend is the Solana deployment of Fluid's Unified Liquidity Layer, which first shipped on Ethereum. It opened publicly in August 2025 as a partnership between Jupiter and Fluid (the former Instadapp team), and DefiLlama still lists a separate Fluid lending protocol on Ethereum. (medium confidence) — https://solanacompass.com/projects/fluid · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://solanafloor.com/news/kamino-drops-liquidation-penalties-90-jupiter-lend-grows, https://cryptobriefing.com/jupiter-lend-overtakes-kamino-solana-lending/, https://api.llama.fi/protocols?own-measurement=lending-by-chain-2026-11-06

## How it works

- [statement] Both v3 and v4 return type(uint256).max as the health factor when an account has no debt (v3 also returns it for an empty user configuration). Integrations that read the health factor must treat max uint as 'no debt', not as a large finite value. (high confidence) — https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/logic/GenericLogic.sol · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://github.com/aave/aave-v4/blob/main/src/spoke/Spoke.sol
- [statement] MixBytes notes that fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens are unsupported by Euler v2 vaults because vaults track balances internally. (low confidence) — https://mixbytes.io/blog/modern-defi-lending-protocols-how-its-made-euler-v2 · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler
- [statement] Gauntlet's curve method applies only to assets with substantial usage data (new assets get a default curve or a comparable live asset) and assumes users are at least partly rate-elastic and that elasticity changes slowly. Its heuristics raise Slope2 and lower the optimal point when whale dominance is high or when supply is large relative to average daily volume or market cap, and lower Slope2 when users are overly sensitive to utilization changes around the optimal point. (low confidence) — https://gauntlet.xyz/resources/methodology-interest-rate-curves · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To vet an Euler vault before depositing, check the factory that deployed it, whether it is upgradeable or finalised (governor set to address(0)), which perspective verifies it, its oracle and unit of account, and which other vaults' shares it accepts as collateral. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/euler-vault-kit/master/docs/whitepaper.md · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://mixbytes.io/blog/modern-defi-lending-protocols-how-its-made-euler-v2

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Aave v3 health factor is the liquidation-threshold-weighted collateral value divided by total debt value: HF = Σ(collateral_value_i × LT_i) / Σ(debt_value_j). A position with HF below 1 can be liquidated. Aave's own example: $10,000 of ETH at an 80% liquidation threshold with $6,000 of GHO borrowed gives HF 1.333. Aave Governance sets the liquidation threshold per collateral asset. (high confidence) — https://aave.com/help/borrowing/liquidations · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://github.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/blob/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/logic/GenericLogic.sol, https://updraft.cyfrin.io/courses/aave-v3/contract-architecture/health-factor

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Euler risk configuration is per vault. Collateral is risk-adjusted by LTV factors, the borrowing LTV must be less than or equal to the liquidation LTV, and LTV ramps affect only liquidation LTVs (new borrows use the new value immediately). (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/euler-vault-kit/master/docs/whitepaper.md · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://mixbytes.io/blog/modern-defi-lending-protocols-how-its-made-euler-v2
- [statement] Design contrast: Compound III is a governance-run product, with fixed single-base-asset deployments whose parameters change only through Timelock proposals. Euler v2 is a permissionless toolkit where anyone can deploy vaults and each vault's governor or curator sets risk. Euler's then-CEO Michael Bentley framed it as 'You can use Euler to build other lending protocols, but the reverse isn't true'. (medium confidence) — https://docs.compound.xyz/governance/ · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://blockworks.com/token-transparency/filing/compound, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/euler-vault-kit/master/docs/whitepaper.md, https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2024-09-04-euler-launches-v2-modular-defi-lending-protocol-following-hack-314655
- [statement] Shared liquidity under isolated front-ends is now a pattern on both chains. Aave V4 uses a Hub and Spoke model in which a Liquidity Hub consolidates liquidity and accounting and Spokes implement modular borrowing with isolated risk. Jupiter Lend's README describes a Liquidity layer shared by Lending and Vaults, each keeping its own risk parameters 'within set limits'. This pairing is analysis, not a claim made by either project. (medium confidence) — https://aave.com/docs/aave-v4 · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Instadapp/fluid-solana-programs/main/README.md, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/architecture
- [statement] Jupiter Lend liquidates by ticks. Positions with similar debt-to-collateral ratios share a tick, and when a tick crosses a vault's Liquidation Threshold all its positions are processed in one transaction. Each liquidation sells only enough collateral to bring the ratio back to the Liquidation Threshold, with a penalty on the liquidated part only that varies by vault. A position beyond the Liquidation Max Limit leaves the tick system and is fully liquidated. (high confidence) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/earn/lend/liquidation-mechanism · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/architecture
- [statement] Blue isolates risk per market in three ways. Borrower collateral stays idle in the contract: `supplyCollateral` credits only the borrower's collateral balance and never the market's lendable supply. Bad debt lands only on the suppliers of the market where it occurred. Blue has no supply caps, so lenders and vault curators control exposure by choosing which markets to fund. The whitepaper argues that skipping re-hypothecation lets markets run at higher average utilization. (high confidence) — https://github.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue/blob/main/morpho-blue-whitepaper.pdf · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue/main/src/Morpho.sol, https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/blue/
- [statement] Morpho Vault V2 replaces the single supply cap per market with adapters, ids and caps. An adapter is a contract that moves assets into one protocol and reports its value through `realAssets()`. The curator can enable new adapters without a vault upgrade. The curator defines abstract `ids` for a risk factor, such as a collateral token, an oracle or a market configuration, and gives each id an absolute or relative cap. A docs example is 'Max 20% of the vault allocated to any market using a specific, new oracle'. The roles are owner, curator, allocator and sentinel. The sentinel can deallocate assets, cut caps and revoke pending actions. (high confidence) — https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/vault-v2 · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://vaultbook.gauntlet.xyz/vaults/morpho-vaults/v2-vaults, https://www.bankless.com/read/morpho-vaults-v2-defi

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] EVC batch() executes several operations atomically and lets account-status and vault-status checks run once, deferred to the end of the call context. Users are expected to go through the EVC's call or batch rather than calling vaults directly, so sub-account and operator authorisation applies. MixBytes likewise describes the EVC as managing accounts, operators and multicalls. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/ethereum-vault-connector/master/docs/whitepaper.md · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://mixbytes.io/blog/modern-defi-lending-protocols-how-its-made-euler-v2
- [statement] Vault V2 can be permissioned with allowlists, unlike non-permissioned V1 vaults. Morpho warns that some gate implementations can stop certain users from depositing or withdrawing, which weakens the non-custodial guarantee. A Fee Wrapper inherits the limits of the vault it wraps, so the underlying vault's gates can block wrapper users even when the wrapper's own gates are abdicated. (medium confidence) — https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/vault-v2 · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://vaultbook.gauntlet.xyz/vaults/morpho-vaults/v2-vaults

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Comet enforces a minimum borrow size, baseBorrowMin: an account's initial borrow must be at least that value, a withdrawal that would leave the borrow below it reverts, and later borrows may be any size. Governance can change the borrow minimum through the Configurator. (medium confidence) — https://docs.compound.xyz/collateral-and-borrowing/ · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://docs.compound.xyz/governance/
- [statement] OpenZeppelin's medium findings show Comet's trust edges: approveThis let the governor approve anyone to move base and collateral assets out of Comet (a governance-attack vector; docstrings were clarified), and a low targetReserves value could stop buyCollateral and leave the protocol holding collateral (the team said targetReserves is meant to be 'a pretty large value'). The governance docs confirm that only the Governor can withdraw reserves or approve manager allowances. (medium confidence) — https://www.openzeppelin.com/news/compound-iii-audit · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://docs.compound.xyz/governance/
- [statement] Anyone can deploy EVK vault proxies through the factory; EVault dispatches some logic to static modules. Upgradeable vaults point at a factory-controlled beacon and immutable vaults use a fixed implementation. A governor can change vault configuration, and setting the governor to address(0) finalises the vault. 'Perspectives' are verifier contracts; the escrowed-collateral perspective requires no borrowing, immutability and finalisation. At launch Euler's frontend supported four vault classes: escrowed collateral, governed, ungoverned and yield aggregator. (high confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/euler-vault-kit/master/docs/whitepaper.md · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2024-09-04-euler-launches-v2-modular-defi-lending-protocol-following-hack-314655, https://mixbytes.io/blog/modern-defi-lending-protocols-how-its-made-euler-v2
- [statement] Jupiter Lend on Solana is built from three programs. Liquidity custodies every token and tracks supply and borrow positions. Lending (Earn, jlTokens) and Vaults (Borrow) hold no tokens and reach Liquidity by cross-program invocation. Each borrow vault has one supply token and one borrow token, and vault positions are represented as NFTs. (high confidence) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/architecture · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Instadapp/fluid-solana-programs/main/README.md
- [statement] Aave V3 E-mode and Kamino elevation groups both restrict borrowing to a related asset set, but they differ in shape. In Aave a user picks one E-mode category, borrowing is then limited to assets in that category, and an asset can belong to several categories. In Kamino a user requests a group, each group names one permitted `debt_reserve`, a market holds up to 32 groups, a reserve can join up to 20, and leaving the group or borrowing outside it restores the per-reserve parameters. (high confidence) — https://aave.com/help/borrowing/e-mode · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://kamino.com/docs/curators/markets/elevation-groups, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kamino-Finance/klend/master/programs/klend/src/utils/consts.rs
- [statement] Euler's vault kit offers IRMLinearKink (utilization = borrows/(cash+borrows) as a uint32; rate = baseRate + util x slope1 up to the kink, then plus (util - kink) x slope2; all four parameters immutable) and IRMAdaptiveCurve, a port of Morpho's adaptive curve that returns per-second rates scaled to RAY for the EVK. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/euler-vault-kit/master/src/InterestRateModels/IRMLinearKink.sol · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/euler-xyz/evk-periphery/master/src/IRM/IRMAdaptiveCurve.sol
- [statement] A Morpho Blue market pairs one loan token with one collateral token. Five parameters define it: loan token, collateral token, oracle address, interest rate model (IRM) address and liquidation LTV (LLTV). The contract stores each market under an id derived from those parameters and has no function that edits them afterwards, so each market is immutable and separate from every other market. (high confidence) — https://github.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue/blob/main/morpho-blue-whitepaper.pdf · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/blue/, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue/main/src/Morpho.sol
- [statement] Vault bad-debt handling differs by version. In V1.0, realized market bad debt lowers the vault share price at once, so all depositors share the loss pro rata. In V1.1 the vault 'does not realize the bad debt': the share price does not fall, and 'the last vault users will face the bad debt unless action is taken'. Anyone, including the curator, can cover the loss by supplying loan tokens. (high confidence) — https://docs.morpho.org/curation/tutorials/bad-debt · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/morpho-org/metamorpho-v1.1/main/README.md
- [statement] A vault counts as a Morpho Vault V2 only if two things hold. It sets its adapter registry to the Morpho Registry, which Morpho governance maintains and which lists Morpho Markets V1 and V2 and Morpho Vaults V1. Its curator also abdicates the ability to change that registry. Before abdication the curator can still change the registry. (high confidence) — https://docs.morpho.org/curate/concepts/adapter-registry/ · keywords: EVM money markets compared with Solana: Aave Morpho Compound Euler · also: https://docs.morpho.org/learn/concepts/vault/
